newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton futures end firm, specs steady buyers.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton futures end firm, specs steady buyers.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed higher, buoyed by speculative buying that emerged at the market's recent lows, traders said.
Benchmark May settled 0.63 cent firmer at 73.98 cents per lb, having ranged from 74.09 to 73.35 cents. The back months closed 0.61 to 0.03 firmer.
Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots compared to Friday's official 23,523 lots.
Support in May was pegged between 73.00 and 72.50 cents. Resistance was seen at 75.50 cents.

Carl Anderson, a cotton marketing specialist with Texas A & M University, said the market may have put in a near-term bottom, adding that the speculators tend to buy the market during this time of year.
But increasing certificated stocks, he said, could put a lid on buying activity. Certificated cotton stocks rose to 202,044 bales of March 21, up from 200,741 bales the previous session.
"What a market for a sadist!," O.A. Cleveland, a cotton marketing specialist with Mississippi State University, said in a weekly comment.
He said technical indicators suggest the May contract could fall below 72.00 cents in the near term. "Hang on. The technicals suggest we are in for a discouraging one to two weeks," Cleveland said.
The industry awaits the U.S. Department of Agriculture's planted area estimate, released next Monday. Analysts expect high soybean and corn prices to dampen growers' enthusiasm for planting cotton.

Anderson said a price around 80.00 cents in new-crop December would make cotton competetive with soybeans and corn. But it may take an estimate below 13.5 million acres for the 1997/98 cotton crop, to spark gains.
December ended at 76.70 cents, 0.50 cent higher.
